'''Larry D. McLerran''' is an American physicist and an academic. He is a professor of physics at the [[University of Washington]].<ref name=yy>{{Cite web|url=https://phys.washington.edu/people/larry-mclerran|title=Larry McLerran &#124; Department of Physics &#124; University of Washington|website=phys.washington.edu}}</ref>

McLerran is most known for his work on particle and [[nuclear physics]], primarily focusing on the [[Color-glass condensate|Color Glass condensate]], the [[Quark–gluon plasma]], and Quarkyonic Matter.<ref name=lk>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=zcxAaxAAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Larry D. McLerran|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

McLerran is the recipient of the 2015 [[Herman Feshbach Prize in Theoretical Nuclear Physics|Herman Feshbach Prize in Theoretical Physics]]<ref name=tt>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm|title=Prize Recipient|website=www.aps.org}}</ref> and the 2021 [[Pomeranchuk Prize]] from the [[Institute for Theoretical and Experimental Physics]].<ref name=ws>{{Cite web|url=https://www.int.washington.edu/about/news-announcements?archived=1|title=News and Announcements &#124; Institute for Nuclear Theory (INT)|website=www.int.washington.edu}}</ref> He is a Foreign Member of the Finnish Academy of Arts and Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://acadsci.fi/jasenet/ulkomaiset-jasenet/|title=Ulkomaiset jäsenet}}</ref>

==Education==
McLerran completed his Bachelor of Science in physics from the University of Washington in 1971. Later in 1975, he obtained a [[PhD]] in Physics from the same institution.<ref name=aa>{{Cite web|url=https://indico.cern.ch/event/820556/page/17060-about-larry-d-mclerran|title=Symposium on Contemporary QCD Physics and Relativistic Nuclear Collisions|website=Indico}}</ref>

==Career==
McLerran was a postdoctoral research associate at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1975 to 1978. Following that, he became a postdoctoral [[research associate]] at the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center from 1978 to 1980. In 1980, he rejoined the University of Washington as an assistant professor, a role he held until 1984. He was subsequently promoted to the position of [[associate professor]] in 1984. He became a scientist in the Theory Division of Fermi National Accelerator Center from 1984 to 1989 and was also an adjunct associate professor at the [[University of Illinois]] from 1984 to 1989. He joined the [[University of Minnesota]] where he served as a professor from 1988 to 2000. In addition to his professorial role, he held concurrent appointments as a member of the [[William I. Fine Theoretical Physics Institute|Fine Theoretical Physics Institute]] at the University of Minnesota from 1989 to 2000 and as visiting professor at the Nordic Institute of Theoretical Physics from 1996 to 1998. From 1999 to 2016, he was a senior scientist at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]. Since 2016, he has been serving as a professor of physics at the University of Washington and a senior fellow of the Institute for Nuclear Theory.<ref name=yy/>

McLerran served as the director of the Theoretical Physics Institute from 1989 to 1992 at the University of Minnesota. From 1999 to 2004, he was theory group leader of the Nuclear Theory Group at Brookhaven National Laboratory, and from 2003 to 2016 he was theory group leader of the [[Riken]] Brookhaven Center at Brookhaven National Laboratory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sciencesprings.wordpress.com/2014/11/18/from-bnl-new-matter-mathematical-models-larry-mclerran/|title=From BNL: "New Matter, Mathematical Models & Larry McLerran"|date=November 18, 2014}}</ref> From 2016 to 2022, he held the position of director at the Institute for Nuclear Theory at the University of Washington.<ref name=aa/>

==Research==
McLerran has conducted research into the characteristics of ultra-relativistic nuclear collisions and the properties of super dense strongly interacting [[matter]]. He has authored numerous publications spanning the areas of [[particle physics]], nuclear physics, and [[Quantum chromodynamics]] including articles in peer-reviewed journals.<ref name=lk/>

===Ultra-relativistic heavy ion collisions and the quark gluon plasma===
McLerran's work on the Quark Gluon Plasma and the theory of heavy ion collisions has made contributions to the field of nuclear and particle physics.<ref name=tt/> His early research explored the theoretical concept of deconfinement of quarks in dense matter. He computed the energy density of a quark gas to the first order where the density dependence of interactions is important,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Freedman |first1=Barry A. |last2=McLerran |first2=Larry D. |title=Fermions and gauge vector mesons at finite temperature and density. III. The ground-state energy of a relativistic quark gas |journal=Physical Review D |date=15 August 1977 |volume=16 |issue=4 |pages=1169–1185 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.16.1169 |bibcode=1977PhRvD..16.1169F }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref> and explored the possibility that such matter may occur in [[neutron star]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Freedman |first1=Barry |last2=McLerran |first2=Larry |title=Quark star phenomenology |journal=Physical Review D |date=15 February 1978 |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=1109–1122 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.17.1109 |bibcode=1978PhRvD..17.1109F }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref> Furthermore, he showed the existence of a confinement-deconfinement [[phase transition]] in a Yang-Mills theory of gluons using Monte-Carlo numerical methods.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=McLerran |first1=Larry D. |last2=Svetitsky |first2=Benjamin |title=A Monte Carlo study of SU(2) Yang-Mills theory at finite temperature |journal=Physics Letters B |date=January 1981 |volume=98 |issue=3 |pages=195–198 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(81)90986-2 |bibcode=1981PhLB...98..195M |osti=1445725 }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=McLerran |first1=Larry D. |last2=Svetitsky |first2=Benjamin |title=Quark liberation at high temperature: A Monte Carlo study of SU(2) gauge theory |journal=Physical Review D |date=15 July 1981 |volume=24 |issue=2 |pages=450–460 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.24.450 |bibcode=1981PhRvD..24..450M }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref> His work also established that energy densities may be large enough and time scales long enough to form a Quark Gluon Plasma in heavy ion collisions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Anishetty |first1=R. |last2=Koehler |first2=P. |last3=McLerran |first3=L. |title=Central collisions between heavy nuclei at extremely high energies: The fragmentation region |journal=Physical Review D |date=December 1980 |volume=22 |issue=11 |pages=2793–2804 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.22.2793 |bibcode=1980PhRvD..22.2793A |osti=1445711 }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref> Additionally, he investigated the emission of photons and dileptons from a quark-gluon plasma and revealed that the emission rates governing the release of photons and dileptons from a quark-gluon plasma are intricately linked to the thermal anticipated value of a correlation function involving electromagnetic currents.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=McLerran |first1=L. D. |last2=Toimela |first2=T. |title=Photon and dilepton emission from the quark-gluon plasma: Some general considerations |journal=Physical Review D |date=February 1985 |volume=31 |issue=3 |pages=545–563 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.31.545 |pmid=9955720 |bibcode=1985PhRvD..31..545M }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref>

===Color glass condensate and the glasma===
McLerran's Color Glass Condensate research illustrated the importance of color electric and magnetic fields inside of strongly interacting particles responsible for particle interactions at high energies. One of the major focuses of his research for the Electron Ion Collider being built at Brookhaven National Laboratory is to explore the consequences of such color electric and magnetic fields.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bnl.gov/eic/|title=Electron-Ion Collider (EIC)|website=www.bnl.gov}}</ref> He and Raju Venugopalan constructed the McLerran-Veungopalan model of strong color electric fields,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=McLerran |first1=Larry |last2=Venugopalan |first2=Raju |title=Computing quark and gluon distribution functions for very large nuclei |journal=Physical Review D |date=March 1994 |volume=49 |issue=5 |pages=2233–2241 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.49.2233 |pmid=10017211 |arxiv=hep-ph/9309289 |bibcode=1994PhRvD..49.2233M }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=McLerran |first1=Larry |last2=Venugopalan |first2=Raju |title=Gluon distribution functions for very large nuclei at small transverse momentum |journal=Physical Review D |date=April 1994 |volume=49 |issue=7 |pages=3352–3355 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.49.3352 |pmid=10017329 |arxiv=hep-ph/9311205 |bibcode=1994PhRvD..49.3352M }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref> and then formulated a mathematical equation that delineated the quantum evolution of the effective theory concerning the Color Glass Condensate (CGC).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Iancu |first1=Edmond |last2=Leonidov |first2=Andrei |last3=McLerran |first3=Larry |title=Nonlinear gluon evolution in the color glass condensate: I |journal=Nuclear Physics A |date=September 2001 |volume=692 |issue=3–4 |pages=583–645 |doi=10.1016/S0375-9474(01)00642-X |arxiv=hep-ph/0011241 |bibcode=2001NuPhA.692..583I }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref> Focusing on nonlinear gluon evolution in the color glass condensate, his study enhanced comprehension of small-x hadronic physics in the high gluon density regime by deriving a functional Fokker-Planck equation and presented the [[renormalization group]] equation (RGE) for the Color Glass Condensate, governing its rapidity evolution.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ferreiro |first1=Elena |last2=Iancu |first2=Edmond |last3=Leonidov |first3=Andrei |last4=McLerran |first4=Larry |title=Nonlinear gluon evolution in the color glass condensate: II |journal=Nuclear Physics A |date=May 2002 |volume=703 |issue=1–2 |pages=489–538 |doi=10.1016/S0375-9474(01)01329-X |arxiv=hep-ph/0109115 |bibcode=2002NuPhA.703..489F }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref> The Color Glass Condensate provided initial conditions for the matter formed in heavy ion collisions, and the early [[time evolution]] of such matter towards the formation of a Quark Gluon Plasma was the subject of his work on the Glasma.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kovner |first1=Alex |last2=McLerran |first2=Larry |last3=Weigert |first3=Heribert |title=Gluon production from non-Abelian Weizsäcker-Williams fields in nucleus-nucleus collisions |journal=Physical Review D |date=December 1995 |volume=52 |issue=11 |pages=6231–6237 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.52.6231 |pmid=10019162 |arxiv=hep-ph/9502289 |bibcode=1995PhRvD..52.6231K }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kovner |first1=Alex |last2=McLerran |first2=Larry |last3=Weigert |first3=Heribert |title=Gluon production at high transverse momentum in the McLerran-Venugopalan model of nuclear structure functions |journal=Physical Review D |date=October 1995 |volume=52 |issue=7 |pages=3809–3814 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.52.3809 |pmid=10019607 |arxiv=hep-ph/9505320 |bibcode=1995PhRvD..52.3809K }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref>

===Topological excitations and high density matter===
McLerran used properties of topological excitations, instantons and sphalerons, in electroweak theory to compute the rate of electroweak [[baryon number]] violation.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Arnold |first1=Peter |last2=McLerran |first2=Larry |title=Sphalerons, small fluctuations, and baryon-number violation in electroweak theory |journal=Physical Review D |date=15 July 1987 |volume=36 |issue=2 |pages=581–595 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.36.581 |pmid=9958202 |bibcode=1987PhRvD..36..581A }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Arnold |first1=Peter |last2=McLerran |first2=Larry |title=The sphaleron strikes back: A response to objections to the sphaleron approximation |journal=Physical Review D |date=15 February 1988 |volume=37 |issue=4 |pages=1020–1029 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.37.1020 |pmid=9958773 |bibcode=1988PhRvD..37.1020A }}</ref> With Kharzeev and Warringa, he developed insight into the effect of topological anomalous effects in strongly interacting theory, the [[Chiral magnetic effect|Chiral Magnetic Effect]] wherein a polarize system and [[electric field]] is generated parallel to an externally applied magnetic field.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kharzeev |first1=Dmitri E. |last2=McLerran |first2=Larry D. |last3=Warringa |first3=Harmen J. |title=The effects of topological charge change in heavy ion collisions: 'Event by event and violation' |journal=Nuclear Physics A |date=May 2008 |volume=803 |issue=3–4 |pages=227–253 |doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysa.2008.02.298 |arxiv=0711.0950 |bibcode=2008NuPhA.803..227K }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref>

===Quarkyonic matter===
McLerran and Pisarski proposed the existence of Quarkyonic Matter, a form of high density matter with quark confinement, yet which largely behaves like a gas of unconfined quarks, which may exist at densities intermediate between that of [[nuclear matter]] and that of a deconfined Quark Gluon Plasma.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=McLerran |first1=Larry |last2=Pisarski |first2=Robert D. |title=Phases of dense quarks at large |journal=Nuclear Physics A |date=November 2007 |volume=796 |issue=1–4 |pages=83–100 |doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysa.2007.08.013 |arxiv=0706.2191 }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref> Moreover, he and Reddy also argued that Quarkyonic Matter may have the properties needed to explain determinations of neutron star equations of state.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=McLerran |first1=Larry |last2=Reddy |first2=Sanjay |title=Quarkyonic Matter and Neutron Stars |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=26 March 2019 |volume=122 |issue=12 |article-number=122701 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.122.122701 |pmid=30978062 |arxiv=1811.12503 |bibcode=2019PhRvL.122l2701M }}{{psc|date=November 2024}}</ref>
